kuzu_graph.$comment: Graph memory (§4c). Owns its own kuzu database; no external daemon.

$comment: Stateless stdio proxy in front of the SnareVec daemon on 127.0.0.1:8756.
It is stdlib-only, so it needs no venv packages and starts regardless.
IMPORTANT: the daemon idles out and is restarted from the SnareVec
workbench. When it is down this server still connects and still lists
tools, but tool CALLS fail. That is a runtime condition, not a config
error - see TOOLS.md (§5a) for how the assistant should handle it.
Pixel-level GUI control. Runs in its OWN venv (mcps/UACC/.venv), not
the harness venv, because UACC is written against mcp v1 (FastMCP)
while the kuzu server needs mcp v2 (MCPServer). Those cannot coexist
in one interpreter. Separate processes can have separate Pythons -
which is exactly what the MCP boundary buys us, and it matches what
UACC's own uacc-mcp.bat already expects (it looks for %~dp0.venv).
Code intelligence through Neovim's language servers (Neovim 0.12.5,
installed via winget). No Python dependencies: it shells out to
`nvim --headless -l` and parses JSON, the same stdlib-only trade the
SnareVec proxy makes.
codemap.rs answers 'where does X live'; this answers 'what calls X',
which needs real resolution rather than text matching.
It needs a language server per language, and registers only the ones
actually on PATH. rust-analyzer is a rustup SHIM here with no component
behind it - run `rustup component add rust-analyzer` once the network is
up. lsp_status lists what is present and how to add the rest.
Adithya's own nyx-nvim tool layer, exposed over MCP. His repo has the tools
but no MCP entrypoint - at HEAD there is no tool registration in any
language, and INSTALL.md delegates the protocol to the npm
mcp-neovim-server. This file is that missing entrypoint.
It shares the Neovim nvim_lsp keeps warm, and starts it itself if needed.
His get_socket() honours NVIM_SOCKET_PATH but guards it with
os.path.exists(), false for a Windows named pipe - the accessor is replaced
at import rather than patching the clone. His `mcp` package also collides
with the MCP SDK's, so the name is swapped during import and restored.
DISABLED by default because roughly a third of his tools hit Neovim API
changes and return empty or error, and every tool schema is prompt tokens
on every turn. Verified on Neovim 0.12.5:
WORK   open_file, list_open_files, goto_line, search_in_file,
diagnostics_summary, module_structure, file_diagnostics,
and the refactor writers
BROKEN current_context / current_location - his _treesitter.py imports
`nvim-treesitter.ts_utils`, removed in nvim-treesitter v1.0/main
EMPTY  file_symbols, find_symbol_in_workspace, find_todos - his _lsp.py
Lua calls vim.lsp.util.make_position_params() with no arguments,
which Neovim 0.11+ deprecated in favour of an explicit position
encoding, so the request errors inside his pcall and yields {}
Both are fixes to nyx-nvim itself, not to this harness. Until then
nvim_lsp answers the same core questions and is fully verified.
Tick this on per workspace in + menu -> Connectors if you want his layer.
NOTE: the refactor tools WRITE to files.
MCP servers the harness launches as child processes and speaks stdio to.
This is the seam that makes the harness language-agnostic (§2): these are
all Python, the harness is Rust, and neither cares.
Paths are relative to the repo root unless absolute.
